motion.label: Stagger
motion.definition: Animate related items one after another with small delays.
motion.promptInstruction: Use a staggered entrance for grouped cards, nav links, or proof items.

motion.label: Scroll Reveal
motion.definition: Reveal elements as they enter the viewport.
motion.promptInstruction: Use scroll reveal only for section handoff and hierarchy, not every object.

motion.label: Layout Animation
motion.definition: Animate position/size changes so layout changes do not snap.
motion.promptInstruction: Use layout animation when cards expand, filters change, or panels rearrange.

motion.label: Direction Aware Transition
motion.definition: Move content according to navigation direction.
motion.promptInstruction: Make forward/back transitions move in opposite directions to preserve orientation.

motion.label: Shared Element Transition
motion.definition: Carry a visual element between states.
motion.promptInstruction: Connect a thumbnail/card to its detail view using a shared element transition.

motion.label: Crossfade
motion.definition: Fade between two states in the same spatial location.
motion.promptInstruction: Crossfade alternate media/states when motion should feel quiet and continuous.

motion.label: Origin Aware Pop
motion.definition: Scale or reveal from the trigger point.
motion.promptInstruction: Open menus, popovers, and cards from their trigger origin instead of center screen.

motion.label: Parallax Depth
motion.definition: Move foreground/background at different scroll rates.
motion.promptInstruction: Use shallow parallax for atmosphere only when it supports comprehension.

motion.label: Press Feedback
motion.promptInstruction: Add subtle scale/opacity feedback to primary buttons and draggable cards.

motion.label: Kinetic Type
motion.definition: Typography moves as a meaningful visual object.
motion.promptInstruction: Use kinetic typography for the headline or section labels, not body copy.

layout.label: Split Hero
layout.definition: Hero with copy and product/visual proof side by side.
layout.promptInstruction: Use split hero when the product needs immediate explanation and visual proof.

layout.label: Dashboard Proof
layout.definition: Hero or section anchored by realistic app/dashboard surfaces.
layout.promptInstruction: Use dashboard proof with supplied or honest placeholder data, never fake metrics.

layout.label: Editorial Stack
layout.definition: Magazine-like vertical rhythm with strong type and image pacing.
layout.promptInstruction: Use editorial stack for calm premium pages and portfolio/studio narratives.

layout.label: Asymmetric Bento
layout.definition: Uneven grid of feature cards with clear hierarchy.
layout.promptInstruction: Use asymmetric bento for product features when one or two ideas need dominance.

layout.label: Proof Band
layout.promptInstruction: Use proof band directly after the hero to ground claims.

layout.label: Workflow Timeline
layout.definition: Ordered steps showing how the product/process works.
layout.promptInstruction: Use workflow timeline for AI/productivity products where sequence matters.

layout.label: Sticky Scrollytelling
layout.definition: One sticky visual paired with changing text.
layout.promptInstruction: Use sticky scrollytelling for complex products; keep it short and purposeful.

layout.label: Comparison Frame
layout.promptInstruction: Use comparison frame when the value is clearer by contrast.

layout.label: Gallery Rhythm
layout.definition: Repeating image/card rhythm with controlled variation.
layout.promptInstruction: Use gallery rhythm for portfolios, commerce, and visual archives.

layout.label: Command Console
layout.definition: Dense command/product surface with filters, logs, or terminal affordances.
layout.promptInstruction: Use command console for devtools, dashboards, and operational products.

aesthetic.label: Warm Editorial
aesthetic.definition: Paper, ink, precise type, quiet premium surfaces.
aesthetic.promptInstruction: Apply warm editorial tokens when the page should feel calm, designed, and trustworthy.

aesthetic.label: Technical Minimal
aesthetic.promptInstruction: Apply technical minimalism for devtools and B2B apps.

aesthetic.label: Cinematic 3D
aesthetic.definition: Depth, staged lighting, hero object, spatial drama.
aesthetic.promptInstruction: Use cinematic 3D as one focal moment, not a whole-page decoration flood.

aesthetic.label: Luxury Monochrome
aesthetic.definition: High contrast, restrained color, gallery-like pacing.
aesthetic.promptInstruction: Use luxury monochrome for premium commerce, studio, and editorial launches.

aesthetic.label: Playful Tactile
aesthetic.definition: Soft shapes, toy-like feedback, approachable interactions.
aesthetic.promptInstruction: Use playful tactile details for consumer or onboarding flows.

aesthetic.label: Brutalist Utility
aesthetic.definition: Raw mechanical typography, visible structure, utilitarian edges.
aesthetic.promptInstruction: Use brutalist utility when clarity and force matter more than polish.

aesthetic.label: Glass Luminous
aesthetic.definition: Translucent surfaces, blur, glow, layered light.
aesthetic.promptInstruction: Use glass/luminous styling sparingly with readable contrast.

aesthetic.label: Dense Dashboard
aesthetic.promptInstruction: Use dense dashboard styling when many states must remain visible.

quality.label: Hierarchy
quality.definition: Clear first, second, and third attention targets.
quality.promptInstruction: Make the first viewport explain product, audience, and value before decorative detail.

quality.label: Spatial Consistency
quality.definition: Related objects keep consistent spacing, alignment, and motion paths.
quality.promptInstruction: Preserve spacing and movement logic across sections.

quality.label: Affordance
quality.definition: Interactive elements look and behave like they can be used.
quality.promptInstruction: Buttons, filters, and cards need clear hover/focus/press states.

quality.label: Contrast
quality.definition: Text and controls remain readable against their surfaces.
quality.promptInstruction: Keep accessible contrast; do not sacrifice legibility for glow or glass.

quality.label: Rhythm
quality.definition: Repeated spacing/type/media patterns create readable flow.
quality.promptInstruction: Use repeated section rhythm, then break it intentionally for emphasis.

quality.label: Content Density
quality.definition: Amount of information matches the product and viewport.
quality.promptInstruction: Avoid sparse dashboard cards or overstuffed hero copy.

quality.label: Information Scent
quality.definition: Users can predict what clicking/scanning will reveal.
quality.promptInstruction: Name sections and CTAs specifically, not with generic marketing filler.

quality.label: Mobile Composition
quality.definition: Mobile is intentionally redesigned, not accidentally collapsed.
quality.promptInstruction: Define mobile order, sticky areas, and motion reductions explicitly.

content.label: Specific Promise
content.definition: Concrete value proposition instead of generic adjectives.
content.promptInstruction: Write the hero around a specific product promise and user outcome.

content.label: Credible Proof
content.promptInstruction: Use real screenshots, workflow examples, customer logos, or honest placeholders.

content.label: Section Contract
content.definition: Each section has a distinct job.
content.promptInstruction: Assign every section a purpose: explain, prove, compare, convert, or support.

content.label: Anti Filler Copy
content.definition: No vague AI-powered/next-gen wording unless expanded.
content.promptInstruction: Replace broad slogans with concrete product behavior and user benefit.

content.label: Implementation Constraints
content.definition: Output format, framework, accessibility, and responsiveness rules.
content.promptInstruction: State exact deliverable constraints so agents produce usable code.

content.label: Source Attribution
content.promptInstruction: Mention Framewell references by title and role in the generated brief.

roles.label: Dominant Structure
roles.definition: Defines the full page skeleton or primary section order.
roles.usage: Use as the main blueprint; other prompts should support it.

roles.label: Hero Concept
roles.definition: Defines the above-the-fold idea, headline/visual relationship, or hero motion.
roles.usage: Use for first impression only unless it is also a full-page structure.

roles.label: Visual Skin
roles.definition: Defines color, typography, texture, atmosphere, or brand feel.
roles.usage: Borrow its surface language without copying unrelated layout.

roles.label: Motion Layer
roles.definition: Defines animation behavior, timing, transitions, or scroll/hover system.
roles.usage: Borrow motion vocabulary and orchestration, not all visuals.

roles.label: Section Pattern
roles.definition: Defines a reusable page section such as features, proof, pricing, FAQ, workflow.
roles.usage: Slot into the dominant structure where that section belongs.

roles.label: Component Accent
roles.definition: Defines a small component or microinteraction.
roles.usage: Use as accent detail only; never let it dominate a page.

roles.label: Anti Pattern Guardrail
roles.definition: Useful mainly as something to constrain, avoid, or demote.
roles.usage: Use as a warning when it conflicts with the selected outcome or vibe.

goodPairs: Quiet premium pages with readable rhythm.
Devtool pages need dense clarity before decoration.
One hero object can anchor a product promise.
Metrics and proof should reinforce each other.
Sequential content benefits from staged reveal.
Bento grids feel better when rearrangement is animated.
Premium commerce/studio pages rely on pacing and restraint.
Consumer flows benefit from physical interaction feedback.
Cards expanding into detail views keep spatial continuity.
A claim should be followed by believable evidence.
badPairs: Too much spectacle can make operational UI feel fake.
Glass effects often damage readability unless tightly constrained.
Raw utility and quiet luxury need a deliberate bridge, not a direct mashup.
Small components should not define a whole website.
Moving type conflicts with dense reading tasks.
Parallax often breaks mobile unless reduced or disabled.
Abstract 3D cannot replace concrete product proof.
Blurred translucent layers make dashboards hard to scan.
Long stagger sequences slow down dense interfaces.
Spectacle can hide weak copy; force specificity first.
